subtopics.title: The Normal Force and the Free-Body Diagram

questions.question: The normal force is defined as the force a surface exerts on an object:
options: Always equal to the object's weight

questions.question: A 50 kg crate on a level floor is pulled by a 100 N rope at 30° ABOVE the horizontal. The normal force is:
If the same 100 N force is instead pushed DOWNWARD at 30° to the horizontal, the normal force becomes:
Why does a wrong normal force ruin the rest of a Newton's laws question?
options: Because the weight is calculated from it
Because the acceleration is measured in newtons
Because it changes the mass of the object
Because friction is calculated from N, so every friction value afterwards is wrong

questions.question: Static friction differs from kinetic friction chiefly because static friction:
options: Is always larger than the applied force
Self-adjusts to match the applied force, up to a maximum of μsN
Has units of newtons per kilogram

questions.question: A 50 kg crate has μs = 0,4. The maximum static friction is:
That crate is pushed with 150 N and does not move. The friction acting on it is:
With μk = 0,3 and a 200 N applied force, the crate's acceleration is:

subtopics.title: Resolving Weight on an Inclined Plane

questions.question: On an inclined plane the recommended axes are:
options: Parallel to the slope and perpendicular to the slope
Along the weight and along the normal force

questions.question: The component of the weight pulling an object down a slope of angle θ is:
On an incline, the normal force is:
options: Equal to mg, as on level ground
Greater than mg because the slope adds a push
Zero, because the object is free to slide
Equal to mg cosθ, and therefore always less than the weight

questions.question: On a free-body diagram for a crate on a ramp, the weight arrow points:
options: Straight down, vertically, regardless of the slope
Opposite the normal force along the ramp

subtopics.title: Worked Incline Problems — Sliding, Held and Pushed

questions.question: A 20 kg crate on a 30° ramp: the component of weight down the slope is:
For that crate the normal force is:
With μk = 0,25 the crate slides down with an acceleration of:
To drag the crate UP the same ramp at constant velocity, the tension needed is:
options: 140,4 N, because friction now acts down the slope alongside the weight component
55,6 N, because friction helps the worker
98 N, because friction does not act at constant velocity
196 N, the full weight of the crate

subtopics.title: Grip, and Why It Runs Out

questions.question: The wardrobe feels easier to push once it starts moving because:
options: Sliding friction is weaker than the static grip that had to be broken

questions.question: Friction depends on:
options: The surface area of contact only
How rough the surfaces are and how hard they are pressed together
The speed of the object only

questions.question: Pushing a 50 kg crate (μs = 0,4) with 150 N produces:
options: Motion, with 147 N of kinetic friction
No motion, and friction of exactly 150 N
No motion, and friction of exactly 196 N

subtopics.title: Gravity Split into Down-the-Slope and Into-the-Slope

questions.question: On a slope, gravity's single downward pull is shared between:
options: A part that slides the object down the ramp and a part that presses it into the ramp
A part that lifts the object and a part that pushes it sideways

questions.question: For a 196 N crate on a 30° ramp, the pressing pile (and therefore the ramp's push back) is:
A steeper hill gives LESS grip because:
options: The coefficient of friction changes with angle
More of gravity goes into sliding and less into pressing, so the surface pushes back less
The weight of the object decreases on a slope
Friction acts perpendicular to the slope

questions.question: Which is the safe way to decide between sine and cosine on an incline?
options: Sine is always the bigger component
Use sine for the normal force, cosine for the slide
Sketch the triangle and check which side leans against the marked angle
Use whichever makes the answer positive

subtopics.title: Will It Slide? The Quick Test

questions.question: The slipping test compares:
options: The weight with the normal force
The mass with the coefficient of friction
The sliding component of the weight with the maximum grip, μsN

questions.question: For the depot crate, 98 N of slide against 93,3 N of grip means:
options: The crate slides down the ramp
The crate accelerates up the ramp
The crate's mass must be increased

questions.question: When the crate is pulled UP the ramp, friction:
options: Grows larger because the pull is larger
Turns around and acts down the slope, with the same magnitude

questions.question: The mass-free slipping shortcut says an object slips when:
options: mg sinθ is less than mg cosθ
